P1.evidence: No setter call to read back. Frame two-part as everywhere else in this batch — 'I just want to get a good idea of where you're at, really understand what it is you want to accomplish as well, and we can build that out. And then if there's alignment, we can obviously talk about the coaching' — with no 'what's in the way' and no 'what you need'. Agreement was 'All righty. Cool.' Open question run verbatim.

P2.evidence: P2d is the best injury question in the batch and it was well timed off a cue: 'When you say you feel your age, just so I'm clear, is there specific areas of the body which are not quite up to standard, having any pains or discomforts or anything like that?' It produced the sciatica disclosure directly. Everything around it is thin. Age was volunteered; height and weight were never established at all on a call that closed at $6,000. Health conditions were never asked. Most striking, the diet question was never asked — the prospect volunteered 'Diet is a part of it. I've been inconsistent with my diet' and the rep then sold a nutrition pillar and promised 'diet's locked' without ever learning what the man eats. Sleep and energy absent as always.

P3.evidence: The opening goal question ran cleanly — 'You said you want to kind of get to the next level. What does that look like? What are we really going for?' — and produced the mirror, the abs, the 20-to-10 target and the peak-at-50 vision. Then it stopped. No bridge question, no 'what does that do for you', no 'who else does that impact' — on a call with a wife pursuing the same goals and three children in the room of the conversation. The reflect-back at 00:10:10 was thin and, worse, it deflected: 'obviously, you want that to be addressed as well, but it sounds like the main focus is just being the best you can be' moved past the sciatica the rep had just uncovered. The prospect supplied his own identity material — 'I turn 49 at the end of June', 'the clock's ticking' — and none of it was laddered.

P4.evidence: The root-cause question ran properly and got a real answer: 'What do you feel like has been the biggest reason why you haven't got to the 10% yet?... What do you feel like has really been the challenge or the barrier for you?' → 'I think it's structure. Diet is a part of it. I've been inconsistent with my diet... my work life has been very consuming up until recently.' The gap was named by the prospect in his own words, which is exactly what P4e asks for. What never ran was the history: what he has actually tried before, what happened to it, and the 'the information isn't the problem, why can't you stick to it on your own?' close-out.

P5.evidence: Absent, and it was handed to him twice. 'The clock's ticking' drew 'Time flies, right?' and 'I'm not getting any younger... this vision of being at a peak point when I turn 50' drew nothing. A 48-year-old with a self-imposed deadline eighteen months out is the easiest consequence frame available and no version of the two-year question was asked. It closed anyway, which is precisely why this should be coached — the phase was skipped and the outcome hides it.

P6.evidence: 'How do you feel about it in terms of a process?' → 'Yeah, I feel good. I'm excited about it' is a soft proxy for the belief check and it did run before the price. The all-in question never ran in any form. 'Ready to rock and roll?' came after the number and is a close, not a commitment check, so the playbook's sequencing — genuine verbal yes BEFORE presenting anything — was not followed even though the answer would almost certainly have been yes.

P11.evidence: The onboarding step was run properly for once — calendar worked through live, Thursday to Saturday ruled out, Monday 2pm Mountain agreed, duration set at 30 to 45 minutes, and contact details verified including catching that the application email was a spam address. Payment reached the link stage on Visa before the recorder was stopped. But no agreement email was mentioned, nothing was signed on the call, and there was no welcome email, no Skool link and no onboarding questionnaire — three of the four scripted steps absent on a closed deal.

objection_plays.detail: No deliberation was requested at any point; the prospect describes himself as someone who pulls the trigger fast.
A wife is present in the conversation and pursuing similar goals, but she was never invoked as a decision gate.
No money objection. $6,000 drew 'Okay. Okay.' and an immediate question about tax treatment — the prospect was asking how to optimise the purchase, not whether to make it.
Timing worked in the seller's favour — he had just freed up capacity and had a self-imposed deadline at 50.
No fear or doubt; the only uncertainty expressed was about kettlebell technique, which the offer answers.

The clinical script gap again. The prospect disclosed sciatic symptoms reproducible on loaded lifting, which is a direct programme-fit question for a training system built on ballistic hinging. There is no scripted screening move, so the rep did the opposite of screening — he converted it into a deliverable, quoting the price with 'for you, it's making sure diet's locked, backs fixed, progressing' and citing his own scoliosis as proof: 'my back used to be screwed, but because of kettlebells... I don't have any back issues anymore.'

notes: The cleanest close in the batch and one of the weaker processes — no objection was ever raised, so nothing was tested, and Phase 5 was skipped entirely on a man who twice said the clock was ticking. Two coaching points. He uncovered sciatica with a genuinely good question and then talked past it and promised to fix it; that is the moment to stop and ask who has looked at the back. And he sold a tailored nutrition plan without ever asking what the prospect currently eats.
